title: How to Start a $1M Online Business WITHOUT "Gimmicks"!
promo_conflict: The host promotes Link Whisper, his own product, and describes its earnings and affiliate program.

idea.name: One-page exact-match niche websites
idea.one_liner: Publish single-page sites targeting narrow search terms, attract search traffic and earn through ads.
idea.customer: Search visitors and advertisers; specific audience not stated.
idea.offer: One-page articles targeting a specific low-competition keyword and exact-match domain.
idea.revenue_model: Google AdSense earnings; other monetization is not stated.

key_quotes.quote: These websites would only be one page, and the keyword I was targeting was also an exact match domain.
Just targeting low competition keyword by the exact match domain, write an article targeting that one very specific keyword and voila.
I was making $10,000 to $20,000 per month from these niche sites by 2011, and so I quit my corporate job.

claims.claim: The host says his niche sites made $10,000 to $20,000 per month by 2011.
claims.quote: I was making $10,000 to $20,000 per month from these niche sites by 2011

acquisition_channels.details: Targeted low-competition keywords and exact-match domains to rank in Google.

ideas.delivery: The host published one-page articles on niche websites; Google sent search visitors and AdSense monetized the pages.

idea.name: Niche SaaS spun off from an underserved feature
idea.one_liner: Turn an underserved feature from a large software product into a better niche product and charge users a monthly fee.
idea.customer: Users who need the underserved feature; exact customer group is not stated.
idea.offer: A standalone software product built from an improved, underserved feature.
idea.revenue_model: A small monthly fee; amount is not stated.

key_quotes.quote: Often they'll have a few features that aren't really their core product that's almost feels like an add-on.
You take this underserved feature, make sure there's a market for it, and you slice it off into its own niche product.
You make this feature way better than the big company, and now you have a viable product that others might be willing to pay a small monthly fee to use.

claims.claim: The speaker recommends reviewing multi-million- or multi-billion-dollar software companies for potential features to spin off.
claims.quote: look for multi-million or even multi-billion dollar software companies and review all the features they have.

claims.claim: The speaker suggests users might pay a small monthly fee for the niche software product.
claims.quote: others might be willing to pay a small monthly fee to use.

ideas.delivery: Build and deliver a standalone software product; the feature, market and delivery details depend on the chosen product.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR may apply to customer data; DMCC Act consumer subscription requirements may apply if sold to UK consumers on subscription terms.
